items.question: How should the system execute Solver and Data Analyst scripts locally?
items.reason: Arbitrary code execution on the user's host machine is a major security risk.
items.whyNow: Arbitrary code execution on the user's host machine is a major security risk.
items.impact: Affects application containerization requirements and installation difficulty.
items.recommendation: (Recommended) Host Execution with User Review: Preview code and filesystem modifications before running locally on the user's machine.
items.recommendationReason: Provides the lowest barrier to setup for local-first execution while maintaining user awareness of actions.

options.label: Host Execution with User Review: Preview code and filesystem modifications before running locally on the user's machine.
options.impact: Easy setup but relies on the user to catch security/infinite loop issues.

options.label: Sandboxed/Containerized Execution: Run all Python/Solver scripts inside a lightweight Docker container or virtual sandbox.
options.impact: Guarantees local host safety, but requires Docker/sandbox dependencies installed on the user system.

options.label: Implicit Execution: Run scripts silently in the background to minimize user input prompts.
options.impact: Lowest friction, but highest security risk if agents produce hazardous code.

items.question: At what granularity should the Orchestrator halt and request human validation?
items.reason: Defines the fundamental interaction model: too many prompts cause user fatigue; too few prompts allow error propagation.
items.whyNow: Defines the fundamental interaction model: too many prompts cause user fatigue; too few prompts allow error propagation.
items.impact: Orchestration state machine logic cannot be finalized without knowing the gating mechanism.
items.recommendation: (Recommended) Stage-Gated Milestones: The orchestrator runs complete phases (e.g., Problem Analysis) and pauses for approval before starting the next.
items.recommendationReason: Strikes the best balance between autonomous agent progress and early error prevention.

options.label: Stage-Gated Milestones: Pause only after major phases (e.g., formulation, coding, validation) for structured sign-offs.
options.impact: Provides structured UX checkpoints but might require rollbacks if early errors went unnoticed during a phase.

options.label: Step-by-Step Approval: Pause after every agent action (e.g., model suggestion, file parsing) for real-time validation.
options.impact: High user fatigue but ensures maximum correctness and fine-grained oversight.

options.label: Post-Execution Batch Review: Run full end-to-end flow to draft paper/code, then let user modify specific parts later.
options.impact: Low friction, but high probability of wasted API calls and compounding errors.

items.question: How configurable should the agent roles and workflows be?
items.reason: Determines product complexity: a rigid structure is easier to refine, while a dynamic one accommodates custom tasks.
items.whyNow: Determines product complexity: a rigid structure is easier to refine, while a dynamic one accommodates custom tasks.
items.impact: Affects configurability requirements and configuration parser complexity.
items.recommendation: (Recommended) Preset Roles with Prompt Templates: Predefine the 9 roles, but allow editing system prompts via local config files.
items.recommendationReason: Ensures the system remains easy to use out of the box while allowing prompt tuning for advanced users.

options.label: Editable Preset Roles: Fixed 9-agent role map, but users can edit system prompts and supply custom tool scripts in a folder.
options.impact: Low friction, high stability; prompts can be tailored by users.

options.label: Fully Dynamic Graph: Users define arbitrary agents, system prompts, and task dependencies in a configuration file.
options.impact: Maximum flexibility for generic multi-agent coordination, but higher setup complexity.

options.label: Closed Presets: Fixed agent descriptions, prompts, and tools to maintain optimal and verified behavior.
options.impact: Easiest to support and optimize, but restricts customization.

items.question: How should the human apply modifications to intermediate agent outputs?
items.reason: Affects UI design and state mutation logic (direct source edits vs chat-based regeneration).
items.whyNow: Affects UI design and state mutation logic (direct source edits vs chat-based regeneration).
items.impact: Frontend complexity and orchestrator state update logic are highly dependent on this choice.
items.recommendation: (Recommended) Hybrid Editing: Allow the human to directly edit text/formulas/code, or provide natural language feedback for agents to rebuild.
items.recommendationReason: Ensures minor fixes are fast (direct edit), while complex adjustments are handled easily via agent reasoning (chat feedback).

options.label: Hybrid (Direct Edit & Chat Feedback): User can directly edit any file or state key OR enter text chat to request changes.
options.impact: Provides maximum flexibility but requires robust synchronization to prevent conflicts between human edits and agent state.

options.label: Chat/Prompt Only: User cannot edit state directly; all changes must be requested through natural language prompts.
options.impact: Guarantees state consistency managed by the agents, but can be frustrating for simple syntax fixes.

options.label: Direct File Edits Only: The UI is a viewer and code/text files are modified strictly through external editors.
options.impact: Simplifies the UI to a dashboard but lacks integrated agent modification workflows.

items.question: What is the primary document compilation target for the Analyst/Writer agent?
items.reason: Determines the generation templates and required local compiler dependencies.
items.whyNow: Determines the generation templates and required local compiler dependencies.
items.impact: Affects the requirements of the Analyst/Writer agent and compiler tools.
items.recommendation: (Recommended) LaTeX compilation from structured Markdown source files.
items.recommendationReason: LaTeX is standard for math competitions and ensures publication-quality mathematical formulas.

options.label: Markdown to LaTeX/PDF: Write in Markdown with embedded math, compiling to professional PDF via local LaTeX template.
options.impact: Excellent for math rendering; requires local TeX compiler setup (or cloud compiler API).

options.label: Microsoft Word (docx): Generate structured Word files with tables and embedded figures.
options.impact: Easier for non-technical or corporate sharing, but inferior math typesetting.

options.label: Jupyter Notebook (ipynb): Output executable notebooks containing explanations, code, and figures.
options.impact: Great for interactive data science, but not suitable for formal paper submission.

items.question: What is the trust policy for API keys and data sharing?
items.reason: Important for compliance with competition rules or corporate data protection.
items.whyNow: Important for compliance with competition rules or corporate data protection.
items.impact: Affects LLM routing architecture, model optimizations (local vs cloud API), and user privacy promises.
items.recommendation: (Recommended) BYOK Local Key Storage: User supplies keys locally, system talks directly to provider APIs.
items.recommendationReason: Provides cost efficiency, flexibility of models, and direct trust without middleman servers.

options.label: BYOK Local Key: Users store their own API keys locally (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) to communicate directly with model providers.
options.impact: Requires user setup and active API accounts; data is sent to model provider APIs.

options.label: Fully Local/Offline LLM: Run local models (e.g., Llama 3 via Ollama) locally on the host machine.
options.impact: 100% private and offline-capable, but requires powerful local hardware (GPU) and models might have lower reasoning capabilities.

options.label: Hosted Subscription: Centralized API endpoints managed by the system provider.
options.impact: No setup friction, but introduces subscription cost and middleman trust boundaries.

items.question: Who is the primary target user segment for this mathematical modeling system?
items.reason: Determines whether we optimize for academic/competition constraints (LaTeX, rapid draft, standard models) or industry workflows (custom databases, production deployment, long-term state).
items.whyNow: Determines whether we optimize for academic/competition constraints (LaTeX, rapid draft, standard models) or industry workflows (custom databases, production deployment, long-term state).
items.impact: Delays in defining core features like document templates and enterprise integration hooks.
items.recommendation: (Recommended) Competition Students: High emphasis on rapid iteration, LaTeX paper template compilation, and standard science libraries.
items.recommendationReason: Modeling competitions have rigid workflows and strict deadlines where agent coordination and paper templating add the highest value.

options.label: Competition Students: Optimizes for rapid turnaround, LaTeX paper template compilation, and standard Python solvers.
options.impact: Simplifies target tools but limits viability for enterprise production environments.

options.label: Industry Practitioners: Optimizes for long-term project persistence, enterprise database connectors, custom domain models, and high security environments.
options.impact: Increases integration and security overhead, requiring longer time-to-market.

items.question: How should the Data Analyst obtain datasets and external literature?
items.reason: Defines the API integrations and data storage capabilities needed in the system.
items.whyNow: Defines the API integrations and data storage capabilities needed in the system.
items.impact: Affects agent tool integration scope and API dependency requirements.
items.recommendation: (Recommended) Local Upload + Web Search: User uploads datasets locally, and agents search the web for missing parameters/facts.
items.recommendationReason: Modeling challenges are usually centered around user-provided datasets, while web search handles supplemental info.

options.label: Local Upload & Web Search: Clean user-supplied files and supplement via generic web searches.
options.impact: Flexible and fits most competition setups; web search tools must be robust to noise.

options.label: Local Files Only: Disable external web retrieval to maintain complete isolation and avoid search API dependency.
options.impact: Very secure and fast, but limits the agent's ability to find parameter values or external references.

options.label: Structured Database Connectors: Native integrations with SQL databases, Kaggle, or academic repository APIs.
options.impact: Powerful for professional environments, but overkill for MVP.

items.question: What level of granularity is required for state rollback and versioning?
items.reason: Impacts how the state database or folder structure stores step history.
items.whyNow: Impacts how the state database or folder structure stores step history.
items.impact: Influences local file structures and history storage design.
items.recommendation: (Recommended) Milestone Snapshots: Save snapshots only at human approval checkpoints to roll back to major phases.
items.recommendationReason: Corresponds to the natural workflow of modeling and prevents minor agent errors from causing full resets.

options.label: Milestone Snapshots: Revert to the start of any completed/approved phase, discarding subsequent state keys.
options.impact: Keeps history clean and manageable, matching the natural human decision gate cycle.

options.label: Fine-Grained Transaction History: Save every agent turn, enabling Git-like diffs, branching, and rewinding to any point.
options.impact: High complexity and disk storage; potentially overwhelming user experience.

options.label: Linear Undo/Redo: Simple single-step rollbacks without version management.
options.impact: Simple to implement, but limits user ability to jump back several steps to re-explore a model variant.

items.question: Which solver stacks should be pre-integrated and supported out-of-the-box?
items.reason: Determines target modeling capabilities (e.g. Optimization, Simulation, Statistics) and local installation requirements.
items.whyNow: Determines target modeling capabilities (e.g. Optimization, Simulation, Statistics) and local installation requirements.
items.impact: Affects standard environment setup scripts and target problem domains.
items.recommendation: (Recommended) Standard Scientific Python Stack: SciPy, pandas, CVXPY, OR-Tools, and NetworkX.
items.recommendationReason: Covers standard modeling domains (linear, non-linear, networks, data) with open-source tools that don't require commercial licenses.

options.label: Standard Python Stack: Bundled support for SciPy, pandas, statsmodels, CVXPY, and Google OR-Tools.
options.impact: Zero cost, covers most academic problems, easy local pip installation.

options.label: Commercial Solver Hooks: Integrate configs to link with Gurobi, CPLEX, or MATLAB.
options.impact: Unlocks high-performance optimization, but requires users to manage external licenses.

options.label: Mathematical Formulation Only: Agents only formulate math models; code execution is entirely up to the human.
options.impact: Minimizes environment dependencies, but reduces system capability significantly.
